authorship: independent literal oracle; every pre-state put and every expected_input field written by hand from assembler-proposal-v1 (sections 2-8), assembler-owner-scope-v2 (A1-A5), assembler-readset-v2, assembler-readset-v3 and assembler-owner-addendum-v3; python used only to parse/expand JSON states and to compare raw_action with raw-descriptors.json; no crates/ source, product assembler, model, codec or test output was read or executed
schema: same case/pre-state format as rich/rich-normal-2.json and boundaries/cases.json (derived pre-state = base + exact JSON-pointer put on the fully expanded base; identities are [kind,actor,slot,engine,session,nonce,generation]); each case additionally carries a one-line 'purpose' as in boundaries/cases.json

prestates.classification: hand-specified history A1 Begin (context n1, T n1, RW3 u1-u3) then A0 Begin (context n2, T n2, RW3 u4-u6); actor1's transaction has the LOWER nonce but the HIGHER identity key (session2 > session1); every identity listed; no model execution or reachability run

hand-specified history A1 Begin (T n1, RW3 u1-u3) then A0 Prepare DmlN0 slot0 (p1, b1, Plan u4, Binding u5); actor0 autocommit On without a transaction, so an authenticated Dml Execute supplies a prospective implicit RW T n2 whose identity key sorts before actor1's T n1; no model execution

post-state of asm/supplement/census-key-order-a0-rollback (A0 Rollback Incomplete first fence, two new O and two new Recovery in transaction identity-key order) plus the actor1 frame handoff applied to owners/obligation disposition only (actor1 RW3+Recovery Transferred to its O, as in rich:recovery-transferred); session/actor/fact effects of that CloseSession are not modelled because the Recovery read-set does not read them; no model execution

Recovery read-set workspace: same as supplement:two-obligations-fenced but the two obligation nonces are swapped (actor1's O is nonce1 in table slot 1, actor0's O is nonce2 in table slot 2) and every O reference (T.obligation, transferred current_holder, fact membership) is updated; table/nonce order now differs from full identity-key order. Reachable only under the alternative nonce-order census reading, not under the key-order reading chosen in notes; used solely to make the Recovery obligation sort observable; no model execution

hand-specified history A0 Begin (explicit RW T n1, RW3 u1-u3) then A0 Prepare SelectN1 slot0 (p1 n1/gen1, ReadyUnbound, Plan u4, no binding) then A0 Prepare DmlN0 into the same slot0 (p1 Retired/SlotReuse, Plan u4 Released; p2 n2/gen2 Current, binding b1, Plan u5, Binding u6). Issued0 resolves to the retired N1 statement, Issued1 to the current one; actor0 still has a live RW transaction so any wrong authentication/census is observable; no model execution

hand-specified history A0 Begin (explicit RW T n1, RW3 u1-u3) then Prepare SelectN0 slot0 (c2, p1, b1, Plan u4, Binding u5) then Execute Success (c3, R n1/gen1, cursor u6-u8, fact f1) then CloseResult Normal (c4, descriptor Closed but still public-current, cursor released, fact f2); next Context 5 keeps the fresh Context under cap; no model execution

cases.purpose: first-fence census with two RW transactions whose nonce order (actor1 T n1, actor0 T n2) differs from identity-key order; cause=actor0 (NCR), peer=actor1 (T.decision); new O and Recovery nonces assigned in transaction identity-key order, rows sorted by full key

same two-transaction census caused by actor1: identical O/Recovery identities and row order, but cause/peer known_decision roles swap (actor1 O NCR, actor0 O NotAttempted) and context/transaction come from actor1

authenticated Dml Execute UndoIncomplete with a prospective implicit RW T n2 plus peer actor1 T n1: phase order new RW3 (u6-u8) then Recovery in transaction identity-key order (prospective actor0 T first: u9, then actor1: u10); cause Plan/Binding not in census
same census for PublicationPending: cause O known_decision Committed while the peer new O keeps actor1 T.decision NotAttempted (A5); new durable receipt in the prospective T scope and new anchor

Recovery Exact on an engine with two Outstanding O from two actors; RWO(E) released, actor0 rows before=T (Held), actor1 rows before=O (Transferred); O rows keep their original known_decision; sorted by full key
MissingFirst removes sorted index0 (actor0 O) only; owner rows unchanged and still link the removed O
ExtraNeverIssued appends a copy of the first row with identity.nonce 255 at the END (a re-sort would place it at index1, before the session2 O)
ForeignEngineFirst rewrites only identity.engine of index0 to 255 and keeps it in place (a re-sort would move it after the engine1 O)
DuplicateFirst inserts an exact copy of index0 at index1 (not appended, not deduplicated): [O_a0, O_a0, O_a1]
obligation table order (nonce1=actor1, nonce2=actor0) differs from full-key order; Exact must list actor0 O (nonce2, session1) before actor1 O (nonce1, session2)
MissingFirst on the swapped table deletes the key-sorted first row (actor0 O nonce2), not the lowest-nonce/table-first row (actor1 O nonce1)
Execute Success on the Retired (slot-reused) Select statement: target bytes kept, AuthNone, so transaction None (not actor0's live T), no cursor/RW births, Env class Execute0 kept
Execute UndoIncomplete on the Retired statement: A2 suppresses the whole census although actor0 holds a live RW T (owners/O empty, transaction None), raw cleanup2/commit1 kept
BindAll SuccessA on the Retired N1 statement: unauthenticated, so A1 empty payload (an authenticated N1 would give Utf8 61); env None
CloseStatement Normal on the Retired statement: LocalCleanup envelope kept, transaction None, owners empty (the current slot0 statement's Plan/Binding u5/u6 must not be released)

control: Issued1 is the current Dml statement in the reused slot, so it authenticates; existing explicit T n1 selected (no T candidate), single-T census with new O and Recovery u7; Plan/Binding not included

Execute Success Select under an existing explicit RW T with a Closed but still public-current old descriptor: no Transaction candidate/RW3, retirement offset1 so new Result nonce2/generation 2+1=3, cursor3 u9-u11

notes: N1 (main ambiguity) 'transaction numeric order' is read as the Identity::key() integer-tuple order (kind, engine, session, actor, slot, nonce, generation) of the transaction identity, NOT the bare transaction nonce. Basis: identity-transition-v1.md:47 says the first-fence Recovery order is '해당 transaction exact identity 숫자순' (numeric order of the exact identity), wire-proposal-v2.md:13 defines numeric order as that integer tuple, assembler-readset-v1.md:28 says '같은 후보 집합은 numeric identity순으로 처리', and assembler-proposal-v1 section 3 says '정상 정렬은 Identity::key()의 정수 tuple'; by contrast resource identities are explicitly ordered by 'global nonce순' (identity-transition-v1.md:37). Within one engine this makes session (then actor) dominate the nonce, so actor0 (session1) T n2 comes before actor1 (session2) T n1 and before a prospective actor0 T.

N2 Consequence of N1: in census-key-order-a0-rollback / -a1-rollback new O are actor0 [10,0,255,1,1,1,0] and actor1 [10,1,255,1,2,2,0], new Recovery actor0 u7 and actor1 u8; in census-new-rw-execute-incomplete / -publication-pending new RW3 are u6-u8, then Recovery actor0 u9 and actor1 u10, O actor0 n1 and actor1 n2. Under the rejected bare-nonce reading the same rows (same sorted positions) would instead carry: A cases O actor1 [10,1,255,1,2,1,0], O actor0 [10,0,255,1,1,2,0], Recovery actor1 [9,1,255,1,2,7,0], actor0 [9,0,255,1,1,8,0]; B cases O actor1 [10,1,255,1,2,1,0], O actor0 [10,0,255,1,1,2,0], Recovery actor1 [9,1,255,1,2,9,0], actor0 [9,0,255,1,1,10,0]. A mismatch on exactly these fields means the implementation chose the nonce reading; it needs an owner decision, not a silent fixture edit.

N3 Under N1, new O nonces of one census always coincide with their full-key output order (O identity reuses T's engine/session/actor). The owner rows still show phase/nonce order differing from output order (actor1's lower-nonce RW3 sorts after actor0's rows). To make the Recovery obligation sort observable, supplement:two-obligations-nonce-swapped is an explicitly non-reachable (under N1) read-set workspace whose O table order differs from key order.

N4 Output sort for owners and obligations is the full identity key (kind, engine, session, actor, slot, nonce, generation) per assembler-readset-v2 section 7 ('정상 output owner/O는 최종 full identity key ... 순으로 정렬'); sorting never renumbers identities.

N5 Resource phase order RW3 -> cursor3 -> Recovery (readset-v2 section 7, identity-transition-v1 resource order 3-5): the prospective T's RW3 take next Resource first (u6-u8), Recovery candidates follow (u9,u10).

N6 Census row recipe (proposal section 7 Fence census, wire-proposal-v2.md:169): existing unchanged RW before=after=holder/Held; new Recovery before=None/after=Transaction/Held; RW3 born in the same Incomplete/PublicationPending action before=None/after=new T/Held (not Released, because only Complete abort or implicit Dml commit release them, proposal section 7 first row); every row linked to its T's O; O count/summary computed from the envelope rows (4, AllHeld).

N7 known_decision roles (owner-scope-v2 A5, readset-v2 section 6 table): cause new O from raw class (Rollback Incomplete / Execute UndoIncomplete -> NotCommittedRecoveryRequired, Execute PublicationPending -> Committed); peer new O = pre-state T.decision (NotAttempted); Recovery rows = original O.known_decision (NCR for actor0, NotAttempted for actor1). The cause is the exact selected T (actor.transaction for Rollback, the prospective T for Execute).

N8 Cause Plan/Binding (u4/u5 in supplement:peer-rw-prepared-dml, u5/u6 in the reused-slot state) are not part of the census ('peer Plan/Binding/Cursor는 census에 넣거나 release하지 않는다'; Execute recipes carry no L(P)).

N9 Peer transaction after the first fence (pre-state supplement:two-obligations-fenced): life RecoveryPending, decision/client_knowledge unchanged, obligation linked; peer O creation_reason PeerActiveTransactionAtFence with reason_mask 8 (bit 3). These fields are outside the Recovery read-set except T.obligation and the O tuple.

N10 The actor1 handoff in supplement:two-obligations-fenced follows the rich:recovery-transferred pattern (owners Transferred to O, previous_holder T, transfer_count 1, O disposition AllTransferred; last_fact, session/actor/fact effects not modelled). Recovery before_holder is the current_holder (readset-v2 section 3 '선택 owner의 before는 current_holder'), so actor1 rows have before=O and actor0 rows before=T.

N11 Recovery negatives (proposal section 8 table, readset-v2 section 7): applied after the full-key sort, no re-sort/dedup; ExtraNeverIssued copies the whole first row (known_decision/summary/count) and changes only identity.nonce to 255, appended at the end; ForeignEngineFirst changes only identity.engine to 255 in place; DuplicateFirst inserts an exact copy at index1; owner rows (including their obligation fields pointing at the original O) are byte-identical to Exact.

N12 Recovery fact uses the current (old) engine E1 and next Fact; fresh_engine = next Engine 2 as [1,255,255,2,0,2,0] (proposal section 3 table, engine=nonce); Recovery has context None, actor 255, control Absent/false/false, transaction None.

N13 Issued[k] resolves by global issue_ordinal k+1 without life/current filtering (raw-selector-owner-scope-v2), so Issued0 in the reused slot returns the Retired statement [3,0,0,1,1,1,1]. Authentication requires the exact issued id to be the current slot statement (proposal section 3 'statement는 원 issued ID+current slot 연결'; 'retired ... target은 인증 대상 없음'); the slot now holds [3,0,0,1,1,2,2], so AuthNone: transaction None, owners/O empty and no peer/self census even for UndoIncomplete with a live RW T (owner-scope-v2 A2).

N14 Unauthenticated Execute Env classes (proposal section 6, A2 '원 class 및 명시 receipt fallback 유지'): Execute0 -> work 1/0, cleanup 255, commit 255, receipt None (no selected implicit-RW T); Execute8 -> cleanup 2, commit 1. Fact candidate is still supplied.
N15 A1: BindAll SuccessA on an unauthenticated target supplies an empty payload; the retired statement is deliberately N1 (parameter_count 1) so that a wrong authentication would show Utf8 61.

N16 Unauthenticated CloseStatement Normal keeps the LocalCleanup envelope (cleanup 1, commit 255, fact candidate) with transaction None and no L(P) rows; the current statement's Plan/Binding in the same slot are not touched.

N17 Retired-statement pre-state history choices not read by the assembler: Prepare SelectN1 creates only a Plan owner and leaves the slot ReadyUnbound (identity-transition 'Prepare N1은 binding=None·ReadyUnbound'); slot reuse retires the old statement with retirement SlotReuse and releases its Plan; the new statement takes generation next_statement_generation=2.

N18 Result generation for select-closed-current-explicit: old descriptor Closed but issued result and descriptor public_generation_live=true, so retirement_offset 1 (readset-v2 section 7 table: 'current Closed는 아직 current public token이므로1'); candidate generation = slot next_result_generation 2 + 1 = 3, nonce = next Result 2. Existing explicit T is selected, so neither Transaction candidate nor RW3 birth; only cursor3 births (proposal section 7 'Execute Success Select').

N19 Receipt/anchor in census-new-rw-execute-publication-pending: new durable receipt in the selected (prospective) T scope [8,0,255,1,1,1,0] and anchor in its engine [12,255,255,1,0,1,0] (proposal section 3 table); cleanup 255 / commit 8 per the Execute8/9/10 row.

N20 Pre-states use only 'put' (no 'remove'); derived states are written with fully expanded identity arrays. Classification strings state which are hand-specified histories and which are read-set workspaces; none is a model-run reachability claim.
N21 Each case carries an extra 'purpose' string (precedent: boundaries/cases.json). A harness that requires exactly {id, pre_state, raw_index, raw_action, expected_input} should ignore or strip it.
